kind: Reused synthetic development fixtures; official documentation verified September 7, 2026. No runtime tests.

cases.question: A deployment workflow uses a shared concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: false. If more runs arrive while one is active, will every waiting run execute? How can I keep several runs waiting, and what order can I rely on?
claims: With cancel-in-progress: false, a new run does not cancel the running workflow through this concurrency setting, but it can replace a pending run. Qualification: The group and repository scope is given later in the original; this is not a guarantee against unrelated cancellation.
queue: single is the default and permits one pending run per concurrency group; a new arrival cancels and replaces that pending run.
The described contention operates among runs sharing a concurrency group in the same repository.
queue: max retains up to 100 pending runs in a group and cancels additional arrivals once the queue is full.

Queued runs are processed in the order they start waiting on the concurrency group; workflow dispatch order is not guaranteed. Qualification: They means retained waiting runs, not the rejected arrivals immediately before this sentence.

Keeping cancel-in-progress: false is compatible with queue: max; combining queue: max and cancel-in-progress: true causes workflow validation to fail. Qualification: Explicit false is a valid configuration choice, not a claim that the property must be written when omitted.
With the default queue, cancel-in-progress: true also cancels the currently running workflow in the concurrency group.

Disabling cancellation of in-progress runs alone does not guarantee execution of every waiting run. Qualification: Inference from pending replacement and the bounded queue; protects refers only to cancellation by this setting.

cases.question: A Python worker batch should cancel its other workers when one child raises ValueError, while still allowing cleanup to finish. How does asyncio.TaskGroup report failures to the caller, and should a worker suppress CancelledError during cleanup? Please include the minimum Python version.
claims: An ordinary child exception such as ValueError causes TaskGroup to cancel the remaining children.

Non-cancellation failures consisting entirely of ordinary exceptions are reported together in an ExceptionGroup after all child tasks finish. Qualification: This means reporting the failures after waiting, not postponing the cancellation request. The special KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit behavior is retained later.
Child coroutines should place cleanup in try/finally; cancellation raises asyncio.CancelledError at the next opportunity.

Explicitly caught CancelledError should generally be propagated after cleanup; swallowing it can interfere with TaskGroup behavior. Qualification: Generally must be preserved; the advice is not an absolute ban on every intentional suppression use case.

A child's CancelledError alone does not trigger cancellation of siblings. Qualification: Applies to the individual child cancellation trigger; it does not claim external cancellation of the group cannot cancel other tasks.
BaseExceptionGroup is used when the collected failures require that group type.
For KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit, TaskGroup cancels and waits for the remaining children, then re-raises the initial exception instead of grouping it.
Further tasks cannot be added after the first non-cancellation failure.
